title: A kernel transform is an equivalence only when it has an inverse
status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
summary: On a two-point space the bounded derived category can be classified completely. Equivalences permute the two simple objects and shift them; a shift-and-swap gives an exact involution.
definitions: Letk be a field andD=Dᵇ(Vec_k×Vec_k), represented by pairs of bounded finite-dimensional complexes.
Write[1] for the cohomological shift. Each complex over a field is isomorphic in the derived category to the direct sum of its cohomology spaces placed in their degrees.
The simple objects areS₁=(k,0),S₂=(0,k). Their shifts are the indecomposable objects, and different simples have no morphisms in any degree.

result.name: Classification in a finite derived model
result.statement: Everyk-linear triangulated equivalence ofD permutesS₁,S₂ and assigns an integer shift to each. In particularF(V,W)=(W[1],V[−1]) is an equivalence withF²≅Id.
result.proof: Split every differential into its image, a complement in its kernel and a remaining complement; the image/complement pairs form contractible two-term summands. This leaves precisely the graded cohomology, proving the decomposition. An equivalence preserves indecomposability and all graded morphism spaces. It therefore sends eachS_i to a shifted simple. The two images cannot be shifts of the same simple, since then some shifted morphism between them would be nonzero although everyHom(S₁,S₂[n]) vanishes. Essential surjectivity forces both simple types to occur. Conversely a permutation with prescribed shifts has an inverse permutation with the opposite shifts and acts componentwise on morphisms, so it is an equivalence. For the displayedF, applying it twice cancels both shifts.

example.calculation: F(V,W) has its two-dimensional first component shifted by one and its one-dimensional second component shifted by minus one. title: Noncommutative observables still have identities and symmetries
status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
summary: Commuting self-adjoint matrices admit a common orthonormal eigenbasis. Noncommuting examples retain an identity and can have exact unitary symmetries; their uncertainty is a quantitative statement about a state.
definitions: An observable in this finite model is a self-adjoint complex matrix. Joint diagonalization means one unitary basis makes every matrix diagonal.
Use PauliX=[[0,1],[1,0]],Z=diag(1,−1),Y=[[0,−i],[i,0]], and identityI.
For normalizedψ, variance is(ΔA)²=||(A−〈A〉)ψ||². A symmetry may act by unitary conjugation.

result.statement: A finite commuting family of self-adjoint matrices is simultaneously unitarily diagonalizable. Forψ=(1,i)/√2,ΔX=ΔZ=1 and|〈[X,Z]〉|/2=1, attaining the Robertson lower bound.
result.proof: Diagonalize one self-adjoint matrix. Every matrix commuting with it preserves each eigenspace, becauseA(Bv)=B(Av)=λBv. Restrict the remaining self-adjoint matrices to those invariant eigenspaces and iterate; their orthonormal eigenbases combine into the required basis. Conversely diagonal matrices commute. For the inequality putu=(A−〈A〉)ψ andv=(B−〈B〉)ψ. Cauchy–Schwarz gives||u||||v||≥|Im〈u,v〉|=|〈[A,B]〉|/2. With the statedψ,〈X〉=〈Z〉=0,X²=Z²=I and[X,Z]=−2iY whileYψ=ψ. All claimed numbers follow directly. limits: The finite result does not settle interpretations of quantum measurement or a Platonic ontology. Unbounded observables need common domains; zero commutator expectation in one state does not mean the operators commute.
extension: For an explicit matrix algebra, compute its center and commutant. These identify classical sectors and exact symmetries without assuming that every noncommutative system has the same observable structure. The commutator expectation can vanish in a particular state even for noncommuting operators. For the maximally mixed qubit state I/2, both Pauli variances equal one but the commutator has trace zero. title: Closing a curve is distinct from choosing a polygon or a winding
status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
summary: A loop is a continuous map with equal endpoints; it need not be polygonal or noncontractible. A uniformly close polygonal approximation preserves winding whenever the straight-line interpolation avoids the reference point.
definitions: Letγ:[0,1]→C∖{0} be a closed piecewise smooth curve andd=min_t|γ(t)|>0.

title: A controlled gate is unitary but protection needs an error model

summary: CNOT is an exact permutation unitary and creates an entangled state from a separable input. A telescoping estimate bounds accumulated implementation error, but unitarity alone does not prove fault tolerance.

Protection is a statement about specified errors, encoding, correction and a performance bound, not merely a name for the intended gate.

result.statement: CNOT²=I andCNOT is unitary. CNOT(H⊗I)|00⟩=(|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2, whose one-qubit marginal isI/2. The two circuit products differ by at mostΣ_jε_j.
